title: From Bain to the Boardroom: Indian-American Arpan Sheth Takes the Helm at NAVEX
excerpt: The appointment of a former Bain & Company senior partner as CEO of a leading compliance-tech firm adds to the growing roster of Indian-origin executives running American enterprise software companies
body:
The list of Indian-origin chief executives steering major American technology firms grew a little longer this month. On May 7, NAVEX — a Lake Oswego, Oregon-based company whose governance, risk and compliance (GRC) software serves some 13,000 organisations worldwide — announced it had tapped Arpan Sheth as its new chief executive officer. Sheth arrives from Bain & Company, where he spent more than two decades advising global enterprises on growth strategy, large-scale transformation and operational excellence.

## A quiet giant of compliance tech

NAVEX may lack the name recognition of a Google or a Microsoft, but its footprint is formidable. The company's platform underpins ethics hotlines, policy management, third-party risk screening and regulatory-compliance workflows at corporations spanning financial services, healthcare and manufacturing. In a post-pandemic world of tightening regulation — from the EU's Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive to America's evolving whistleblower protections — the demand for such tooling has surged. Revenue in the broader GRC software market is expected to exceed $20 billion by 2028.

Sheth's mandate is to accelerate that trajectory by weaving artificial intelligence more deeply into NAVEX's product suite. The firm has already begun embedding machine-learning models to flag anomalous third-party transactions and to triage whistleblower reports by severity. Under Sheth, it plans to expand those capabilities while pushing into new geographies.

## The Indian-American executive wave

Sheth's appointment fits a pattern that has become impossible to ignore. Sundar Pichai at Alphabet, Satya Nadella at Microsoft, Arvind Krishna at IBM, Shantanu Narayen at Adobe, Raghu Raghuram until recently at VMware — the list of Indian-born or Indian-origin leaders at the apex of American tech is long and getting longer. What distinguishes the latest cohort is the broadening of sectors. Compliance technology, fintech infrastructure and health-tech platforms are now joining the traditional strongholds of cloud computing and consumer internet.

For the Indian diaspora, these appointments carry significance beyond corporate optics. They validate a pipeline that stretches from the Indian Institutes of Technology and Indian Institutes of Management through elite Western graduate programmes to the upper echelons of American business. Bain & Company, where Sheth built his career, has long been a crucible for such talent, and his ascent mirrors the trajectories of several desi executives who moved from consulting into operating roles.

## What NAVEX's bet signals

The choice of a strategist rather than a product engineer to lead NAVEX hints at the company's priorities. With its core technology mature and its customer base large, growth is likely to come from disciplined geographic expansion — particularly into the Asia-Pacific region, where regulatory complexity is intensifying — and from acquisitions that bolt on adjacent capabilities such as ESG reporting and supply-chain transparency.

For Indian-American professionals in the GRC and legal-tech spaces, the appointment is a signal that the corner office is no longer reserved for a narrow archetype. And for NRIs watching from Mumbai or Bengaluru, it is a fresh data point in an increasingly persuasive case: that the American technology industry, whatever its other faults, remains a remarkably meritocratic arena for Indian talent.

Jon Campo, previously NAVEX's senior vice-president of finance, has been promoted to chief financial officer as part of the leadership transition. The company's private-equity backers at Thoma Bravo, which acquired NAVEX in a deal that valued the firm at roughly $5.5 billion, have signalled confidence in the new team's ability to push the next phase of growth.
nri_angle: Indian-American executives continue to ascend to the top of US enterprise tech. Sheth's appointment at NAVEX extends the pattern beyond consumer tech into compliance and regulatory software, validating the IIT-to-consulting-to-CEO pipeline that many NRIs follow.
author: Diaspora Desk
